hints: Look closely at the graph around 1963 when vaccination was introduced, cases fall from about 400 000 to near zero and stay low, so think about what a vaccine actually puts into the body.

Remember the difference for measles vaccine: does it give you ready-made antibodies for a short time, or does it make your own lymphocytes respond and remember for a long time, and what does that mean for hosts available to the virus?
walkthrough:
**Observe what the graph is telling us**

Look at the sharp, sustained fall after vaccination was introduced in the early 1960s. This is not a small yearly wobble, it is a long term drop to almost zero cases. That tells us transmission of the virus has been interrupted.

**Recall what a vaccine does**

A measles vaccine contains weakened or harmless antigen, not ready-made antibody. Your own B and T lymphocytes respond, make plasma cells, antibodies and memory cells. That is the definition of artificial active immunity, which is long lasting. It is not artificial passive immunity, which is given antibodies directly and is short lived.

**Link immunity to fewer hosts**

When many people are immune, the virus cannot easily find a susceptible person to infect and reproduce in. Fewer people can act as hosts, so even unvaccinated people are protected. This is herd immunity, and it explains why cases stay so low after the vaccine programme.

options.A: Correct, vaccines give artificial active immunity (yes), not artificial passive immunity (no), and immune people reduce the number of hosts so transmission falls (yes).
options.B: False, a vaccine does not provide artificial passive immunity because no ready-made antibodies are injected, it makes you make your own response.
options.C: False, it is wrong on both first ideas, vaccines do not give passive immunity and it is not true that host numbers stay unchanged when so many become immune.
options.D: False, it correctly says artificial active immunity but wrongly says fewer people as hosts is no, when herd immunity is a major reason cases stay low.
